conventions.convention: Credibility requires a product-measurable membership graph and posterior mass at least 1−γ on the declared data domain. Coverage is fixed-truth sampling probability. Honesty uses liminf inf coverage; exact calibration uses uniform absolute coverage error.

The empirical-Bayes selector maximizes the actual score series on [0,A], with explicit full-measure domain and measurability hypotheses. Its zero-selector branch is all of ℓ² and asserts no ℓ² posterior at α=0.
The hyperrectangle bounds sup_i i^(1+2β)θ_i² by M; the open problem instead uses a Sobolev ellipsoid bounded by R². The polished-tail block includes both endpoints N and floor(ρN).
Every truth class in the open problem satisfies θ₁=0, and admissible credible sets are arbitrary graph-measurable subsets of ℓ², without a ball or closed-set restriction.

load_bearing.statement: At a fixed truth θ∈Θ, frequentist coverage is c_n(θ):=P_{θ,n}{y:θ∈C_n(y)}. Posterior credibility requires a measurable membership graph and posterior mass at least 1−γ on the declared data domain.

For every fixed L≥1, the constructed sparse-gap truth belongs to Θ_β(M), has θ₀,₁=0, is outside every fixed polished-tail class, and has subsequence coverage tending to zero, under the stated model, cap and radius hypotheses.

concerns.concern: The unrestricted set formulation appears to admit an affirmative construction, undermining its unresolved status. Let B_n be the inflated empirical-Bayes ball with uniform coverage tending to one supplied by the cited polished-tail theorem, choosing inflation at least one. The cited paper also supplies its no-log Sobolev radius bound in Theorem 3.13 and the complete proof in §7; the bounds can be uniformized over the stated compact β interval. Put H={u∈ℓ²:u₁=0} and E_n={√n X₁≤Φ⁻¹(1−γ)}. Every allowed truth lies in H, and P_θ(E_n)=1−γ exactly. On positive-selector data define C_n=B_n on E_n and C_n=B_n\H otherwise. The positive-α posterior assigns H mass zero because its first coordinate is a nondegenerate Gaussian. Thus this graph-measurable deletion preserves posterior mass and cannot increase diameter. On the zero-selector branch retain ℓ²; its probability tends uniformly to zero by the same radius/lower-bracket estimates. Consequently the uniform coverage error is bounded by the uniform noncoverage probability of B_n plus the zero-selector probability, and tends to zero. Independence between E_n and B_n is unnecessary. Source checked: [Szabó, van der Vaart and van Zanten, Theorems 3.6 and 3.13, §7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1310.4489v5), including the complete short proof of Theorem 3.13. The added nonzero-norm restriction does not prevent this construction.

seams_checked.note: The white-noise supplier gives independent Gaussian coordinates and distinguishes cylinder observations from Hilbert-valued white noise. The owned sequence formulation preserves these distinctions. The coefficient and finite-truncation diagrams agree with their maps.

The owned definition supplies a proper posterior kernel rather than inferring one from an arbitrary potential. This respects the prerequisite's distinction between positive-finite-evidence fiberwise normalization and a data-indexed conditional-law version.

The open problem's reference accurately describes contraction through expected posterior tails outside diverging multiples of a rate. It does not claim that the prerequisite's second-moment/contraction result establishes exact frequentist coverage.
